review_text: This is a great place to visit as you enter the Valley of the Moon area. It is an interesting area to look at. There is a salt caverns that you can go through though I’d definitely recommend going through it with a guide for safety reasons. Things to know before you go: this cavern is not a good place for people with knee issues or other skeletal issues to try to walk/hike through. You have to lean way over while crouching so as not to hit your head on overhead rocks while also using both hands to brace against the rocks on the side while walking over incline surfaces and trying to hold your flashlight and camera. But if you are agile enough to do all those things it was an interesting 20 minute trek through the cavern. Take lots of water, sunscreen and a hat.

review_text: What an experience! My girlfriend and I went on the Old Santiago tour and the Wine-bike tour in late May 2009. A must go, if you enjoy biking and a tour guide (Andres) that is so passionate about Santiago and the surrounds. It's no wonder this is the #1 attraction in Santiago, Chile. Old Santiago Tour: Andres is all about demonstrating both sides of the city. A mixture of the beautiful and picturesque is contrasted with the scars left behind from Santiago's sometimes brutal recent history. Being an architect, Andres pays special attention to how the various structures and buildings around town were made. The trip is well paced, very safe, and is very suited to cyclists of all levels. This tour is best enjoyed early on in your trip to Santiago so that you may have time to go back through the city and revisit the places you enjoyed the most. Wine tour: Andres again has devised a tour that demonstrates contrasts. First off, the tour starts at the El Magnolio Bed and Breakfast in Pirque, about a 45 min drive outside the city. We were treated to a wonderful breakfast which served as a good fuel for the bike ride to come. The house is simply magnificent and the owner is lovely and welcoming. You arrive at Concha y Toro (a very large winery with plenty of tours and tourist visitors) for a tour and wine tasting (you get to keep your tasting glass too, as a parting gift, and it's of really good quality). The bike ride thereafter is a bit long for some bikers, but very flat, on a paved road, and with very little traffic, if at all. There are stops along the way to mention some of the nearby houses and other wineries. This was the ride where you could really relax and enjoy the mountain scenery that surrounded you. You arrive at Vina William Fevre (a small winery, closed to tourism) for an exclusive look at the production facility, a bike ride around the actual grape vines (even taste some grapes if they're growing). The lunch at the winemaker's property was fantastic and you could enjoy some bottles of Vina Fevre wine. Both the Old Santiago and Wine tours were in small groups (4 people). Upon returning to Chile I would not hesitate to book another tour with Andres again.

review_text: Disappointingly you cannot go inside without having insider connections. That said it is a place that you should visit, not least because it played a major part in the Pinochet takeover in 1973. Today it is worth going to look at the architecture, see the changing of the guard (check locally for which day this is), the statues at the back and the enormous Chilean flag which makes a great photo if you can catch it in the wind. The cultural centre to the back and underneath La Moneda has to be just about the most boring place we've been in - exhibition included. For a free, great half hour, just sit in the park area in front of the building and watch the people of Santiago pass by - oh and those street dogs ..... How can any South American dog be so fat?

review_text: Most people do this as a late afternoon tour, ending at sunset. I'm sure that's very pretty, but the crowds must be terrible. We went on mountain bikes, starting early and leaving at around 4pm just as dozens and dozens of minibus tours arrived in one massive convoy. Before that, there were only around 15 other people we saw all day. Give it a full day, start early when it's nice and cool, walk up the big dune, go in the canyon and the tunnel carved by the wind. Take as much water as you can carry - there is nothing available in the valley itself, although there are a couple of shelters which are essential for a little respite from the sun. The whole road up the valley is passable by mountain bike, apart from one tiny stretch which was covered in soft sand. Leave by 4pm, and you'll have the place almost to yourself.

review_text: I took this tour the day after Christmas 2022 on a solo trip to South America. I wanted to experience the natural beauty of Chile and get some exercise in so I booked this trip with AndoAndes. Communication was great on the day of the trip. He was joined by two other guides and a driver to support a total party of seven guests. Juan and his companions were very attentive throughout the trip. Juan would visit each of us periodically during the hike all day long just to check in to see how we were doing. Hiking throughout wasn't terribly difficult, but there are some spots that you have to use all four extremities to climb over. I wouldn't recommend it for anyone who isn't in good health or has mobility issues. But if you're moderately healthy, it's a great experience to immerse yourself in the beautiful Chilean countryside. review_text: Our party of six completed an incredible 12 day/11 night Patagonian adventure curated by Carrie and the team at Venture Patagonia. By way of background, we are all in our mid-to-late fifties and were in search of an active, private, multi-sport adventure that would test us but not break us. We considered three other outfitters but ultimately opted for Venture Patagonia since we strongly preferred a company with local presence and knowledge. Carrie helped us customize an itinerary that included horseback riding in an estancia, kayaking, glacier trekking, whitewater rafting and two spectacular hikes (Base of the Towers in Torres del Paine National Park and Laguna de Los Tres in Los Glaciares National Park). As we refined the itinerary, she worked to minimize hotel transfers, create some room for contingencies (never know about the weather) and incorporate time for recovery from our long hikes…all much appreciated. During the trip itself, transfers were smooth as we progressed through our itinerary and Carrie was easily reachable through WhatsApp to help answer questions and confirm activities/reservations for the following day. She was also extremely helpful in setting up airport transfers as well as a day trip to the Colchagua Valley outside of Santiago for some wine tasting. Simply put, we had a blast and credit Carrie and the team at Venture Patagonia for helping us to experience the beauty of the area in so many different ways. If you’re looking for a locally-based outfitter to help you and your travel party get the most out of your time in Chilean/Argentinian Patagonia, give Carrie a hoot, you’ll be in good hands. review_text: We went on the tour on 01/06/2024. Hediberto, our guide, was spectacular! He explained about the formation of mountain ranges on the way up and the difference between the soils at the beginning of the climb and closer to the top. He even showed us a Condor during the climb! Furthermore, he told us interesting facts about the regions of Vale Nevado, Farellones and Colorado. Even how they work in winter for skiing, etc. throughout the tour. In general, the experience was very rich, wonderful and beautiful! First we stopped at a viewpoint and could see the mountain ranges. We stopped in the snowy valley to use the bathrooms and take in the view. It was very foggy there, so we couldn't see many things, but sometimes the sun came out and we could see the mountain ranges. Then, in Colorado, the cable car experience was also very good, there in what they call a refuge house was where we saw the sunset. There we had access to wine (those underage could drink soft drinks) and boards with different cheeses, salami, parma ham, strawberries, grapes and toast. The wine, according to some people, helped to warm up since it is very cold up there. (That's why I think they should tell you to bring a coat and wear warm clothes) Watching the sunset was beautiful, it was a little foggy, but luckily it cleared and we were able to see the sun set and it was incredible! Seeing the mountain ranges behind was really cool! The driver was very good, obeyed the traffic rules and made us feel safe both on the way there and on the way back. Tenha um ótimo dia!

review_text: Of all the places I visited during my week in Santiago, this museum has stayed with me the most. It’s extremely well done, starting on the ground floor with the global context of peace & reconciliation committees around the world, before moving up to the next 2 floors that deal specifically with the Pinochet regime, from the initial coup, to the referendum that saw democracy restored. The information is brought to life in vivid detail with media footage, newspaper front pages, personal testimonies and many personal items from those who suffered under the regime. I chose to go there because I’m interested in political history but of course, once you’re there, it’s impossible not to be moved and upset by the information & testimony of victims of torture, and the children of disappeared parents. All of this was handled as sensitively as it could be, with a memorial space to sit and reflect. Another aspect that I think made it so interesting and widely relevant is that the museum does a good job of giving the global context as well. We learnt about the roles played throughout the regimes duration by other countries, and I was interested in the wall that told how specific countries around the world reacted to the numbers of Chileans seeking political refuge. My only complaint, and it’s a tiny one, was that I was so bowled over by the museum I really wanted to talk through some of the things I’d read and ask a couple of questions but the only staff I could find were at the front desk, who were completely disinterested in talking. My comment that it was a fascinating museum to the man collecting the audio guides just met with a curt yes, before turning his back on me (we spoke in spanish so it wasn’t a language issue.) My top tip would be to take the audio tour unless you’re completely fluent in Spanish as you don’t want to miss out on any of the details, and some panels are only written in Spanish. It’s also worth knowing there’s a fairly nice cafe within the complex, and it’s easily accessible by metro.

review_text: We took the 3pm tour with Franklin on a Saturday. The weekend seemed to be a good choice since the otherwise frantic city center is much more calm. Well, except for the specific Saturday we ended up picking since we ran into a huge Bolivian carneval parade ;) Anyway, the stops of the tour represented a good mixture of "serious" (i.e. places of historic significance - and frequently tragedy) and "entertaining" (trendy neighborhoods, viewpoints etc.). During the highly informative and pleasant 3 1/2h tour Franklin managed to do the near impossible: One one hand he left no doubt about his own qualms with the Pinochet era, the fact that Chile still has the same constitution from back then, and the negative consequences of that fact for current society. On the other hand he always gave room to opposing views without ever suggesting that they don't possess credibility. Combined with the various other insights he provided, this gave us a feeling of true authenticity. While it was obvious that certain deals exist with a few vendors and restaurant owners along the way, there was never any hard selling during the tour. Only a super-quick pitch and on we went. The tour included a scheduled 30min stop at a restaurant, but when no one opted for it, Franklin continued right away and seemed happy to do so, supporting the overall impression that (even the non-paying) customer is king. Nice! In sum: Highly recommendable! Go for it on your first day in the city.

review_text: My wife and I were staying in a wooden chalet near the base of the mountain, so were able to make the short drive to the volcano easily in our hire-car. From here we went for an hour long walk around an interesting side vent volcano. We then, after a picnic lunch on the slopes, took another chair-lift almost to the snow-line. From the upper station it was a 20 minute walk up to view an area of outstanding beauty, with an active glacier grinding away quite close-by us. We did not venture on to the ice itself, as we only had simple boots. Instead we went for a slightly lower level walk around the wonderful volcanic scenery to another sub-peak. We spent 6 hours in total up the mountain, the highlight of our months tour of Chile.

review_text: We turned up here on spec having read that we could do a tour. We had just missed the start of one and were walked round to where it was - no hanging around. The guide was very friendly and keen to make sure we all understood. She spoke a little english but the tour was officially in spanish. The group was two scottish, one american and two french (who spoke some spanish). She did a great job of keeping us all engaged. They also had a fig tree part way round the tour and didn't mind at all when I grabbed a few - delicious. The tour was a little more in depth than the one we had done at Mistral the day before and significant effort went into helping us understand what she was trying to say. At the end we tasted two pisco based sweet drinks (mango+pisco and blueberry+pisco) plus two piscos (a clear one and an oak aged one). The pisco was nice (but I would say personally that I thought the Mistral was a little nicer) and you can't complain for free. As with other places there was no pressure to buy anything after the tour (but everyone did buy a bottle of something). It's a little out of the way to get here. We got the bus to drop us on the main road and then walked a kilometer or so up to the pisqueria. I'm sure taxis were available for little cost if you prefer.

review_text: Signed up for a jaunt up to the summit of Volcan Osorno with Huella Andina. It was unexpectedly more of an adventure than I anticipated and it was also awesome. Apparently only about 500 people do this summit a year, including guides, and when we got up there I had the spectacular views all to myself. We also saw sunrise on the way up which was a beauty. Yes, it's not cheap at all! But against all preceding expectations I ended up thing it was money well spent. There is a government mandated limit of 2 people per guide, and it takes about 10 hours to do, plus my guide was rated 10/10 by me, so I could see where the money was going. It is not a technical assent - unless you request it to be! - but you will need crampons and an ice axe (supplied). Also, I know other people have written that it was really hard, but I didn't believe them, and I was out at the pub until perhaps 3 hours before collection for the trip. Mmm... mistake. It is quite hard even if you think you are fit. You need some sensible polar gear. You should also build some redundancy into your trip to make sure you can go up on a good weather day. Enjoy!

review_text: First of all let me say that you should reserve this well in advance. It was on our list of good wineries to see (since we weren't going to be able to make it across the border to Mendoza), but when we called to make reservations they were all booked, and there was a wedding the next day. HOWEVER, I am glad we decided to go anyway. We wanted to drive up to the Andes and chose to swing by Errazuriz just to see it even if we couldn't get a tour. The wedding had not yet started and they were technically closed, but the staff member (Fernanda) was very nice and gave us a free tour, although no wine-tasting. The winery is gorgeous and my wife and I decided to buy a bottle of their wine to bring back to the states. Moral of the story is, book in advance! But if you can't get a spot and you're in the area, it's still worth showing up.

review_text: What a beautiful place owned by wonderful people! Friends and I went in March 2012 for an afternoon excursion and were greeted by the owner Osvaldo and his wife, Monica. We were given a variety of options of activities- from mountain biking, to horse back riding, to taking a walk with a guide to learn about the local flora and fauna. The walk to the beach was about half an hour through beautiful wetlands. When we got back, a homemade lunch was ready (prepared by Osvaldo himself), made entirely with fresh, organic, local ingredients (even some from his gardens!) The pastel de choclo, seafood soup, and lasagna were incredibly delicious. My friends and I agreed at the end our of semester that this meal was the best one we had in Chile. Osvaldo is an amazing chef! You get an appetizer, entree, and dessert for about 6 mil chilean pesos (about $12 USD). Worth every cent! We didn't stay overnight but we saw the available rooms, and they looked extremely comfortable and reasonably priced. If you go to Viña del Mar/Valparaíso, you don't want to miss out on this beautiful place & amazing food! Great for all ages, for a day or for a week!

review_text: This was a great 1 day tour of Patagonia from the Chile side. Reserving thru tripadvisor was very easy, which redirected me to Viator Travel Agency who eventually sold a Patagonia Planet tour company. We told them our hotel at Puerto Natales and they picked us up around 8:20 am. They immediately gave us a bag of snacks and bottled water. We picked up a few more people and then promptly left for Patagonia. First we visited the Milodon Caves where they found remains of prehistoric Milodon animals. This was pretty cool. Then we went to Grey Lake and was able to see some icebergs, which was also very cool. Then we ate lunch at a cabin. The soup was very good and we had a choice of chicken or steak. I chose the steak and it was very tasty. We saw some eagles and condors landing near the cabin where we ate and got some really awesome pics closeup. Then we left and saw one more lake closer to the twin towers (Torres). This was the place where they take a lot of pics for postcards and it was so picturesque. Our guide Juan Pablo (aka JP) was awesome and explained everything in spanish and english. The driver Alex also was really good. Every stop we made even if it was windy or raining, he would wipe the glass down so we could see clearly out of the van. It was a great tour and an awesome way to see the best of Patagonia in a day. review_text: I just completed a 7 day 6 night ski/snowboard week as arranged by Santiago Aventures. We chose to book a self-guided tour because we wanted a complete skiing/snowboarding experience and read many places that roads can be difficult to drive on. They arranged the week for us and here are the good and bad points. Pros: -They affiliate with Powderlodge in Farrellones and they are an awesome, boutique hotel that is just like being in your ski house but with better cooks -Their driver Chris was great. He was always on time and he gave us lots of interesting information on Chile. He spoke impeccable English. -They provide you with most of the week planned out for you which is what I wanted because I wasn't planning the trip on a whim, (the week before we hiked the Inca Trail to Machu Picchu which had to be booked 6 months in advance) -They readily answer emails and will help figure out an itinerary that works for what you want. Cons: -they do not arrange for a way to get to Valle Nevado from Powderlodge, but Christian (hotel owner) can help you with that. This is a con because my contact agent at Santiago Adventures previously informed me that we could walk to each mountain base and so my husband and I didn't take cash out at the airport. Then, at the mountains, their ATMs didn't have cash either so we almost didn't have a way to get to Valle until Christian helped sort this out. -they should stay more up to date in regards to conditions when their clients are there for the week. We were at El Colorado, Valle Nevado and La Parva where the snow was great. Then, when we went to Portillo and Arpa, the snow was awful. I would have liked to have been told of the poorer snow conditions and given an option to do something else like mountain biking, four-wheel driving, snowmobiling, winery tours, etc. In retrospect, I can say I would have gone to Portillo for the history experience but was bored there after just one day. And Arpa, backcountry skiing that had snow worse than what I experience on the east coast, I would have loved to have been given a choice to do something else had someone offered. They should stay up to date on conditions and offer alternatives as I was bored my second day at Portillo and hated the snow that I rode at Arpa. (I am a snowboarder so maybe skiers liked the icy conditions better but being a season pass holder at Killington for 7 years and knowing how to ride ice, I can say that I actually disliked the conditions at Arpa more.) -My itinerary said that there would be a lunch box for the day we went to Arpa and there wasn't. So my husband and I were in the back country with no food or water all day. We would have brought something had we known but like I said, my itinerary said it would be provided. In conclusion, I would recommend Santiago Adventures if you want your ski trip in Chile planned out for you. They were a good company and offer a good service. My recommendation is that they think a little more in regards to the clients so that a snowboarder like myself, doesn't get stuck at places like Portillo (where it's definitely catered towards skiers-t-bars everywhere) and icy backcountry snow at Arpa. This means that if I hadn't used Santiago Adventures, I would not have done a 2nd day at Portillo and would have checked into how Arpa's snow conditions looked before booking so that I could have done other activities that Chile has to offer.

review_text: We stayed in San Pedro for 6 days and one of the things on our list was El Tatio Geysers. We had our own transport so we were going to self drive. All the advice was to leave by 430am so that you could see the geysers at their best because is coldest at dawn and this means the steam is at highest view volume. However none of us felt like getting up that early and driving in the dark on what we heard was a bad road which would have lots of tourist buses and mini vans on it .... So we left at midday instead and also decided to go via Puritama hot springs which looked like a viable alternative route to el tatio from San Pedro. There was no traffic but the dirt road to Puritama was very bad, rutted, steep uphill, and many stretches of more than 1km where there was only room for 1 vehicle. To top it off there was a precipitous drop on one side. Luckily there was no traffic because I would not have enjoyed reversing down that windy track (downhill vehicles have right of way). After a slow hour we made to to Puritama where no one felt like bathing so we continued on the terrible road towards El Tatio. Wonderful scenery and only saw one other vehicle in 3 hours which is how long it ended up taking. We had a 4wd which was really needed. By the time we got to El Tatio all the crowds had left and we had the place completely to ourselves. While not quite as spectacular as some of the photos it was still really engrossing to wander around observing the many big and some very small geysers and bubbling mud holes (stick to the marked paths !) and being there all by ourselves. The return journey via the recommended route (follow the signs or trust google maps) was much less stressful and much shorter - only 1.5 hours. Also has some great scenery including a flamingo filled lake, hills full of barrel cactus and lots of Vicuña. Bottom line - if you don’t want to get up early and want to avoid crowds El Tatio is well worth visiting in the afternoon !

review_text: We had a private tour for four people that included a visit to Frutillar, a Bavarian-styled village overlooking Lake Llanquiue with a backdrop of the snow-capped volcano, Mt. Osorno. We stopped for a three-course lunch which was included in the tour. It was local fish and quite simple, but good. Lastly, we visited Petrohue Falls and the rapids. It is a long and beautiful cascade with turquoise pools and a backdrop of the Andes and Osorno. The tour was extremely well-planned – great timing, great guide, lovely lunch and beautiful scenery. Veronica and Gail Stein were great communicators throughout and we made it back to the cruise ship with plenty of time to spare.

review_text: The 7 day Torres del Paine W trek starts and finishes at EcoCamp, which is a great experience in itself. It doesn't matter if you are in a Standard dome or a luxurious Suite dome, it's the EcoCamp vibe that leaves a lasting memory. The community domes where groups gather to meet, eat, relax and socialize is the heart of EcoCamp and is where I spent the most time when not on the trail. The food was awesome! The staff were always friendly and helpful. My guides Danny and Paz did a great job keeping us safe on the trail and their knowledge of the geography, plants and wildlife was exceptional. The walking was well paced and not overly demanding although the weather conditions did prevent my group from ascending to the two highest points in the W. The four seasons in one-hour weather is also what keeps this trek interesting. The wind gusts constantly remind you how nature rules in the wilderness. The Torres del Paine W trek should definitely be on your bucket list and Cascada Expediciones offers the perfect way to achieve your goal. review_text: We’ve taken winery tours all around the world, but never seen one like Lapostolle Clos Apalta Winery, outside of Santa Cruz, Chile. This boutique winery was set up by the grand-daughter of the creator of Grand Marnier liquor – Louis Alexandre Marnier Lapostolle. It clearly has been a labor of love for her and she was able to provide strong financial support to the building of this winery. The winery is located on a rural road off of the main highway to Santa Cruz and shares the road with three other very reputable wineries. The tours are limited to eight or less people (we had four) booked in advance by reservation and are available at least in either English or Spanish. Our English tour guide was a former English teacher and was an excellent guide. The winery is about eight floors high, built into rock hillside, so that the wine making process can rely on gravity as much as possible and avoid pumps. The “roof” level is a garden. The tour starts one level below the roof where the grapes that had been hand picked are received and a team of women individually remove the grapes from the stems. The grapes are then taken and lowered by gravity into the primary fermenters, which are oak (unusual in this day of stainless steel primary fermenters). After primary fermentation, the wine is gravity few to the oak casks in the level below. After a year, the casks are taken by elevator to a level below for blending and storage on oak for another couple of years. Finally the aged wine is lowered to the last level for bottling. One of the highlights of the tour is the visit to the “two year aging room” which has a huge glass topped table in the middle to serve as a bar for tasting the wines. While there, the tour guide turns on the lighting under the glass table where you can see the stairs that go down under the glass table (one end cantilevers up to allow the owner to descend the stairwell). The first floor under the table is a “library” of wine bottles that have been given to the owner from other wineries. The second level below the table is another library of wine racks that hold 250 bottles of each vintage that has been produced at the winery. The wines include a 2005 that won the Wine Spectator best red wine in its Top 100 Wine ranking. The only “negative” is that the price of the tour is US$40 per person which sounds very expensive when one compares it to other wineries but given that it is a very restricted tour with a quality guide and you get to try some of the best wines in the world (costing over US$100 per bottle), the admission fee is appropriate.

review_text: If you haven't seen penguins, go! The fishing boats (5000 pesos each) out to the islands go at random times, but sit and have a drink, and you might get on one. Minimum 10 people. We stayed in a cabana, 50m from the seashore. Could hear the waves all night and there was a lovely patio to sit out on. The birdlife all along the beach was superb. campingpandeazucar@hotmail.com or granatacama@gmail.com to book a cabana. We spent weeks trying to find these! The cabanas were basically equipped (no kitchen knife in the one we had and only one wine glass) but were beautiful with the bedroom overlooking the Pacific and a lovely ensuite bathroom. Electricity is from a single solar panel and you can't plug anything extra in. Bring matches, a penknife (with a tin and bottle opener) and a torch. The bed linen was very luxurious. Don't expect hot water all the time or a state of the art shower - you are in the middle of nowhere! If you are bus/taxiing in, bring all your food with you and don't expect to buy anything in the Park. The restaurants in the fishing village are good and very reasonable but if you want breakfast and to do your own thing, bring it with you! A car would have been useful, but as we were only there for 3 nights, we could do all the local walks. We were handed a tsunami leaflet on arrival and this was somewhat unnerving. Chanaral is heavily polluted and we are glad we didn't stop there for long.

The cabanas were basically equipped (no kitchen knife in the one we had and only one wine glass) but were beautiful with the bedroom overlooking the Pacific and a lovely ensuite bathroom. Electricity is from a single solar panel and you can't plug anything extra in. Bring matches, a penknife (with a tin and bottle opener) and a torch. The bed linen was very luxurious. Don't expect hot water all the time or a state of the art shower - you are in the middle of nowhere! If you are bus/taxiing in, bring all your food with you and don't expect to buy anything in the Park. The restaurants in the fishing village are good and very reasonable but if you want breakfast and to do your own thing, bring it with you! A car would have been useful, but as we were only there for 3 nights, we could do all the local walks. We were handed a tsunami leaflet on arrival and this was somewhat unnerving. Chanaral is heavily polluted and we are glad we didn't stop there for long.

review_text: This museum is interesting and thought provoking, well worth the challenges of the layout and systems. It is right by the Quinta Normal metro stop. They ask you for ID when you enter (at least when you get an audio guide). If you don't have anything they recognise (they didn't like my UK passport) you have to fill in a form with your name and address. If you are not a Spanish speaker you will need to have an audio guide at a cost of 20,000 pesos. The layout doesn't seem to follow an obvious route and some of the signs are incorrect. For example, all the signs for the cafe direct you to the third floor. The floor plan of the third floor shows you where the cafe is. Interestingly, the cafe is on the ground floor, outside the main entrance and round the back. It serves cheap refreshments, so worth a visit. The displays themselves are excellent and you learn a lot about the Pinochet era. Moving and thought provoking. Highly recommended.

review_text: We booked two tours online with Chilean Wine Lovers: the first, a tour of three Maipo Valley wineries, the second, a tour of the Emiliana winery on our way to Valparaiso and Vina del Mar. Mauricio was quick to reply and confirm dates, but we had difficulty paying on his site (we found out later that this part of the site was indeed not working), and we were concerned once we arrived that because the payment hadn't worked, there would be no tour. Our followup email to Mauricio, asking what we should do, did not receive a reply, so we were a bit anxious when we reached Santiago. Turns out, there was nothing to worry about - the tour was still on, Mauricio was very relaxed about the payment and the site was fixed by the time we reached Chile. We were on our own with Pablo for both tours, as Mauricio was studying for his winemaker's exams. Pablo was an exceptional guide, versed in the geography, demography and sociology of his country. He was able to answer our many questions, and seemed to know exactly the type of information that would be of interest us! Our first tour combined a small, family-run organic winery, a tour of the notoriously private Perez Cruz operation (only two tours get in per day, we were one of them), and a tour of the sprawling Santa Rita operation. We loved how each tour was different, and we learned different things from each. On Day 2, we toured the Emiliana organic winery in the Casablanca valley, and visited Valparaiso. We enjoyed our time so much at these two locations that we decided to give Vina del Mar a pass. At Emiliana, we were partnered with a group from Canada (where we are from) for the tour. We had a wonderful time with these folks, only to discover during the tasting that they were our flight crew for our return trip in two days! In Valparaiso, we visited Pablo Neruda's unique house, La Sebastiana, and had a wonderful seafood lunch nearby at Oda Pacifica - where we had the best ceviche ever! From there, we scaled two of Valparaiso's hills and took many photos of the amazing murals. It was a wonderful two days with Pablo and should we have the opportunity to return to this amazing country, we will again book a Chilean Wine Lovers' tour!

review_text: Our party of three travelled to Chile in November 2015 and was looking for a good vineyard tour outside of Santiago. We did some research and found O'Higgins Tours based out of Rancagua. Brian was very prompt with his responses and we quickly had a date and time picked--O'Higgins was very accommodating to our schedule. Also, Brian gave us a heads up about the commuter trains being temporarily out of service, and gave us an excellent recommendation for getting a bus to Rancagua. Mauricio picked us up at the bus station in Rancagua right on time. The car ride to the Anakena vineyard took about 45 minutes or so, during which time Mauricio gave us a great introduction to the region and its history. His English is excellent. The Anakena vineyard is breathtakingly beautiful. Acres of vineyards under a clear blue sky, with the Andes in the background. The tour guide at Anakena was also very informative and took us through the whole process from grape to bottle. The tour was capped off with a tasting at their magnificent bar. Their carmenère (varietal which is Chile's specialty) was fantastic. All of us--we three, Mauricio, and the Anakena tour guide (whose name escapes me)--had a great chat during the tasting. Afterwards, Mauricio drove us back to the bus station to complete the tour. I had the sense that it's a little off the beaten path, but in my experience this is usually where you find the most memorable travel moments. And O'Higgins Tours certainly impressed with their knowledgeable personnel and courteous service. I'd recommend these folks in a heartbeat; if ever I find myself in Chile again, I'd definitely do another of their tours. Thank you to Brian and Mauricio for helping to make our trip to Chile a great one!

review_text: We went to Pucon for 3 days and I would almost have to say that it was the best part of our trip. We did not plan anything ahead of time except for the hostel we were staying at. We arrived late in the afternoon and walked around Pucon to get acquainted. We found a little agency off the main road that would take us to Villarica the next morning. They size you for a snowsuit and climbing gear. We needed to bring sunglasses & sunblock (reflection off the snow), bottled water and lunch (sandwiches). We arrived at the agency around 7:00am and arrived at Villarica around 8:00-8:30 by taxivan. We then took a chairlift up to the starting point which was about 10-15min ride. From there you start to climb zig-zag up the mountain. It's cold and scary because all you have keeping you up on the mountain is your boots (only sometimes with snow-picks) and an ice-pick. We rested a couple of times and reached the crater around 12:00-1:00pm. Along the way there were amazing places to take breathtaking pictures. We actually climbed INTO the crater, kept some volcanic rocks and took pictures of the lava splashing up close to us. The smell is a little nausiating but you put up with it because of the experience. On the way back you slide on your bum down the mountain on man-made snowslides. Your pants and bum get wet but it's lots of fun. We arrived back at the agency around 4:30 and immediately made plans to vist the hot springs "Las Termas". Go to the natural ones at the top of the mountain and you'll melt away all the physical discomfort from the day. You should be in pretty good shape to undertake this activity but if your group is too fast for you, slower groups along the way will always welcome an addition. Make sure you go on a clear day-other people who went with us were making it their 2nd trip because the first time they couldn't see anything. Have fun and enjoy!

review_text: Taking this tour with guide Borris and driver Ariel was the perfect introduction to this amazing country. My husband and I got off the plane at 9am, dropped our stuff off at the hotel, and began the tour at 12. The plan was to do anything and everything to stay awake until it was bed time in order to lessen the onset of jet lag. We were in for a real treat and were enthralled with the things we saw on our tour through Santiago. With stops at Santa Lucia Hill, the Bella Vista District, and Santiago's bustling city center, we didn't have time to think about being sleepy. The following day we had another outstanding Servitour experience going to the Andes mountains and its surrounding vibrant communities. Ariel was our driver again (very happy about that...he is phenomenal) but this tour was narrated by Estéban. The descriptions of his experiences hiking and skiing and snowboarding were so interesting to listen to. He is very connected to the earth and I appreciated how he expressed his sacred views of the land. He was knowledgeable and passionate and was an excellent guide! All 3 of our guides spoke English verrrry well. My husband and I appreciated that. Best part of the trip was standing atop a silent mountain and watching the incredible condors gliding in between the Andes’ peaks. Priceless. It is also important to note that I felt safe everywhere I went. Even when I was alone. Take these tours for sure!! Thank you, Ariel, Borris, and Estéban for such great experiences! Dear Mrs, Thank so much for your great comments about your experience with us knowing Santiago. We work everyday to deliver experiences!! We hope to see you again to continue knowing more about Chile and surroundings. Kind regards

review_text: AndoAndes seems like a good company and I wouldn't want to put anyone off trying their other, longer trips - other reviewers are raving about them - but I would advise against the Cajon del Maipo tour unless all you want is a few hours out of the city. The tour is over-priced for what is distinctly underwhelming. Our guide, Lili, was lovely and knowledgeable, and tried hard but had very little to work with. For a start, the cascades that are the object of the trip have dried up. Hardly AndoAndes' fault and, to be fair, they did mention it before booking. But the walk up to the cascades barely qualifies as a "hike" so isn't worth doing without that end point. You're just left looking wistfully at some wet rocks. Admittedly, the view back into the glacial valley was impressive. But lunch after the 'hike' was also underwhelming given the premium price of the tour. It may have been organic but was just some pre-packed sandwiches and fresh fruit. Nothing wrong with it but, when you think what they could have done with some traditional but simple Chilean food ... Dear, We appreciate your words. As a company, we have decided to suspend any new tours to Cajon del Maipo Waterfalls, until the drought that affected us has been corrected and that the river reestablishes its proper course, hopefully with the winter rains (June-July 2012). Besides, we have also defined a standard for all lunches on all tours so that they will have the same quality that has been recommended by our clients on the rest of the tours/excursions. Regards, AndoAndes Team

For a start, the cascades that are the object of the trip have dried up. Hardly AndoAndes' fault and, to be fair, they did mention it before booking. But the walk up to the cascades barely qualifies as a "hike" so isn't worth doing without that end point. You're just left looking wistfully at some wet rocks. Admittedly, the view back into the glacial valley was impressive. But lunch after the 'hike' was also underwhelming given the premium price of the tour. It may have been organic but was just some pre-packed sandwiches and fresh fruit. Nothing wrong with it but, when you think what they could have done with some traditional but simple Chilean food ... Dear, We appreciate your words. As a company, we have decided to suspend any new tours to Cajon del Maipo Waterfalls, until the drought that affected us has been corrected and that the river reestablishes its proper course, hopefully with the winter rains (June-July 2012). Besides, we have also defined a standard for all lunches on all tours so that they will have the same quality that has been recommended by our clients on the rest of the tours/excursions. Regards, AndoAndes Team

review_text: Having some spare days available in Santiago, I decided to book the daytime cooking class (including the visit to the markets), and I was so glad I did. The market tour was an interesting taste of culture in itself, and seeing (and sometimes sampling) the vast array of food items and even simply soaking up the ambience was very enjoyable. The food and drink during the classes were delicious, and I was impressed that the friendly hosts (Connie & Matias) were able to put together a vegetarian option for my Ceviche, substituting mushrooms for the fish. There were a lot of interesting stories shared by the hosts and our group, and lot of laughs as well. A typed copy of the recipes was provided to us all to take home. I would love to attempt them here one day soon to share with my New Zealand family and friends. I would thoroughly recommend these classes as an excellent way to learn about Chilean food and culture, and it was loads of fun at the same time.

review_text: This is an awesome way to spend an afternoon in San Pedro de Atacama. Our tour left at 230pm (I believe there is also a morning tour as well - perhaps seeing the sunrise vs sunset?) Any way, we opted for the sunset and evening tour - - but do not be fooled..the sun is really strong and hot and we wore jeans - mistake! although it did cool off after the sunset ..but that is the end of the trip so you hop on a bus shortly after. I would have definitely wore shorts. Bring plenty of water and it's recommended to even bring a flashlight (we weren't told this and used our cell phone) because you will crawl (yup, hands and knees) through 60 meters of a cave. Kind of cool - but wasn't expecting it so caught us off guard. The scenery is awesome - I won't go into detail cause you can google all of the images. I will say that many of the tours had setup refreshments and snacks at the conclusion of the sunset - ours did not - so ask about that before you book. It looked like a lot of fun and made all the people on trip want to get in on that action. Oh and there is a 3,000 pesos per person. www.noapprovalneeded.com

review_text: I was leary about going to Torres del Paine in the winter because I could find very little information before I left but I'm so glad I went anyway! I flew into Punta Arenas and rented a car to drive myself there. It took me about 4.5 hours but the roads were great. It's a nicely paved highway from Punta Arenas to Puerto Natales then a great dirt/gravel road starting just outside Puerto Natales. I was alone but it was an easy drive and the scenery gave me a great sense of the place and its stark grandness. I spent about a week at the Hosteria Lago Grey which I loved. The place was perhaps 1/4 occupied so I had a nice room with a great view (room 701). I could lie in bed and see the mountains and look across the lake to the glacier. The staff and food were great. I took the boat across the lake to see Glacier Grey on their first trip of the season (when I first arrived the boat wasn't running yet). Cold but beautiful. I did some hiking around the park (no more than a few hours at a time, no major trekking) which was just amazing. I also drove all over the place and, in winter, there were virtually no other people or cars anywhere. I had the whole place to myself so could go as slow as I wanted, stop in the middle of the road, do whatever. It was fantastic! I was even pleasantly surprised by the weather. It was cold now and then but not nearly as cold as I expected. It was often windy but not always. One day it was blowing at least hurricane strength but with 6 days there I had plenty of gorgous sunny days too. The scenery can't be beat! The mountains are truly amazing while the lower parts of the park are easily accessible (no snow on the ground) and gorgeous in all shades of brown and gold before the spring greenery comes. I saw guanacos galore, condors, hawks, foxes (even a family of 4 foxes who live near the hotel!), skunks and even flamingoes! This was the trip of a lifetime and worth every penny I spent to get there (all the way from Hawaii).

Claudio stayed near us at all times, occasionally one of the other guides would go play, it's was fun to watch what they can do in a kayak. If we're ever back in Punta Arenas we'd definitely give Claudio a call and go again.

review_text: We are 9 months into our year ling trip and this tour has been a highlight. The different landscapes and views were breath taking and we lucked into having a lovely group of people in our car and a great driver. Andreas (sp?) our driver was absolutely brilliant, he was a very safe driver in the off road conditions and sure everyone was comfortable as we went along. The food he prepared in the middle of these vast landscapes was delicious and we had more than enough food every meal, he ensured the vegetarians in the group were catered for without hassle. His knowledge of the geography and history of the areas was brilliant and he could even explain some of the basics in English for the non Spanish speakers (us!). He made sure to stop at any particularly picturesque points for “photos photos!” and even took some great perspective shots on the salt flats with his boots and a dinosaur toy he brought along. His playlist in the car was brilliant and he was very funny and warm throughout the whole trip. I was particularly impressed with how attentive he was when a member of group was feeling the effect of the altitude, offering any help/remedies he could and assuring them it would get better as we got lower (which it did!) All in all we wouldn’t hesitate to recommend this company and Andreas to anyone in the future.

review_text: We've been living in Chile for 3 years and have visited the MIM several times with our young children. Having been to many science centers in Canada and the US, the MIM does not compare - it is small and the quality and variety of exhibits pales in comparison. With that said, as far as Chile goes, the MIM is the only venue of its type and can be a great way to pass a rainy / cold day with young children. Our kids particularly love the bubble room, where they can make giant bubbles of different shapes, in some cases encasing themselves in the bubbles. There are a number of other interactive exhibits that really captivate our kids, like construction sites where they can load and transport dirt, balls that balance on upward airstreams, drawing tables, peg boards where you can make hand / body impressions, etc. Upstairs there are also some good exhibits on electricity and outer space. For very young children (under 4 years, I believe), they have an area where they can colour and play simple computer games. There is also a building block area that is similarly tailored to younger children. In addition to the exhibits, they have a daily schedule of workshops and shows you can sign up for as part of the entrance fee. Unfortunately many of the really interesting ones, like building a robot, are only for older children (over 10 years old)... which really disappointed our 6 and 4 year old boys. Occasionally they have workshops for young children (which my kids never find interesting). They also always have some sort of short movie on a specific topic, like dinosaurs or Chile. The movies are somewhat entertaining, but nothing spectacular or memorable. So, if you are travelling to Santiago with young children and have some time to kill and want to spend it in a kid-tailored venue that is educational, the MIM is a viable option. Personally, we continue to go to the MIM for something to do for 3-4 hours with the kids during the shoulder seasons when the weather is poor and ski season is closed. In good weather there are many other more compelling options (beach, parks, hiking in nature parks, Mampato amusement park, etc.) to entertain the kids.

review_text: We booked a day trip to visit the King Penguin colony in Tierra del Fuego. The van picks you up in the early morning around 7:30am; we take the 9am ferry (2 hrs), then a several hour van ride (with some small stops along the way) to arrive at the colony; the total time to arrive there is about 5 hours, and you return by a different route. When we returned to Punta Arenas, it was around 9:30pm, however sometimes due to weather affecting the ferry schedule, this can be potentially much later. Our guide told us that her latest record was returning at 3am, although this was very unusual. It might be a good idea not to have any tight schedule that night or early the next morning. On the way to the penguin colony, we stopped for lunch at a small restaurant, which is at your own expense. You can also buy groceries from a store next to the restaurant. We had a English-speaking guide who was cheerful, attentive, and knowledgeable. The penguin colony has a max of 200 penguins, and around half are at sea at any given time. When we went (late December '16), there were around 60 penguins total. There are 2 lookout points, where you stand behind a barrier and look out at the colony. When we went, the penguins were around 100m away. I would recommend bringing binoculars and plenty of warm clothing. It can get very windy during the 1 hour you have to view the penguins. Our visit was in late December 2016. We saw penguins sitting on their eggs, but no babies. There were some penguins walking to or from the ocean. For the most part, the penguins were not active and stayed in the same place and position. They are very majestic but you will not be able to get up close to them, as this is a protected colony. This colony is very recently formed within the last few years. I saw one fox nearby. This trip may be worthwhile if you're an animal lover or photographer. However, my family enjoyed Isla Magdalenas more because there were baby penguins at this time of year and the penguins were much more active.

review_text: A highlight of South America and one of the most wonderful experiences. We did the 3days / 2 nights tour from San Pedro to Uyuni with World White Tours. You travel by land cruiser with stops across the most beautiful landscape, colourful lagunas, Wild Flamingoes, amazing rock formations, wild llamas in lush Greenland, bathe in hot springs and see the most insane amount of mountains peaks and volcanoes. I had no idea how much beauty Bolivia has, the best was saved to last... the Salt Flats. It’s the most surreal experience, stunning landscape where the skies are reflected, and you play with perspective creating incredible memories and pictures. Although you go as a larger group of about 24 (4 cars) with this tour we experienced a lot of the places alone which was amazing... I’ve never experienced being in such a beautiful place with absolute silence! This might be due to our guide Oscar making sure this happened. You meet up with the other cars in certain locations, so you also have the comfort that you are with a larger group that can help each other out. A massive thank you to our guide Oscar! He made us feel welcome, safe and comfortable throughout, it was a pleasure to spend time with him. He made every effort to make it the best tour (which is was). If you can definitely try to request Oscar as your guide, he does Spanish and English tours. In terms of comfort (I like my comfort...), the land cruiser was fine and lots of fun, we played our own music. The food was great, really filling and good mix of veggies, meats and carbs, defo bring snacks though in case you get hungry before lunch. review_text: We were keen to do this stargazing night and managed to set this up on our last night in San Pedro following some emails back and forth with Jorge. If you are keen to do this (which I highly recommend) then I would suggest contacting Jorge and getting your name down for one of your first nights in San Pedro, as tours depend on cloud conditions and it also costs less per person if there are four or more on the tour. We were slightly apprehensive about paying 80USD seeing as we had no astronomy knowledge at all but it was completely worth it, it was like nothing we had ever done before and was incredibly interesting. The evening started with a pick-up from our hostel at 8pm where we taken to Jorge's compound. The first hour and a half was spent on basic astronomy which was fascinating. After a short break the second hour and a half was spent using the telescopes to observe the stars, planets and the moon and again was fascinating. My wife has a DSLR camera and Jorge was kind enough to spend some time using his equipment to get some photos through the telescope. I would agree with the comment in another review that it might be an improvement to have hot drinks while you are sitting during the astronomy lesson. Whether you have a prior knowledge of astronomy or not, you will find Jorge can tailor the night well and this is must-do in this part of the world with such great stargazing opportunities.

review_text: Overall this is a great excursion to adventure on from Puerto Natales. You get to not only see the beautiful glaciers, but waterfalls, cormorants, and other fauna & flora. I was with my 68 & 69 year old parents who made the hike to see the glacier with no problem. Yes, this is a large boat with a lot of people, but for us it did not distract from the experience. There were three busses waiting to take the passengers to the boat and return to the city in the afternoon. We had no waiting issues as others mentioned. Some have complained about the experience at the Estancia for lunch, but we thought the food was really good. The red wine, not so much, but you have plenty of other beverage choices. No, you don't see them cooking the lamb in the traditional style, but when you're feeding 120 people it doesn't make sense. If you want the Estancia experience, I recommend the full day excursion to Estancia La Peninsula which is wonderful. The staff was friendly and professional. Just a great experience overall. Tip: Be sure to go outside when approaching the waterfalls as the boat gets super close. It's great for pictures and videos.

review_text: I paid for a "tour" for my wife and I to visit the Andes, hoping to stop to take photos and enjoy the scenery along the way. However, as the company name implies, it really isn't for people like us, but for all the Brazilians who show up in Santiago during the winter to ski. If you are NOT skiing, don't take the tour offered by this company. It's a bit deceiving because they do have an English description of the tour in their pamphlet, so on would think that some of their guides would be able to speak English. I tried my best to speak the little spanish that I know, but it was only enough to get picked up and dropped off at my hostel. I knew already it was going to be a long day after the bus ride to the MassKi offices. They asked my wife and I to get up at 7:05am for the bus to pick us up. The driver was on time, but for him to come back to the same exact corner to pick up another couple at 8:10am seemed very silly and inefficient. My wife and I could have gotten another hour of sleep and enjoyed the free breakfast at the hostel we were staying in. We started our day at 7am and ended it at 8pm, which was much longer than expected. Since we didn't ski, we were idle for about 10 hours, either waiting at the ski lodge or sitting on the bus, haha, so it felt like a wasted day. review_text: BirdsChile is a wonderful organization! We only had a couple days to spend in Puerto Varas but they were able to work gracefully with our time crunch. We scheduled a full day tour around the "Lakes District" with a guide named Carlo (who we requested on behalf of other trip-advisor reviews). Carlo spoke fluently in Spanish, English and Italian and was a wonderful guide and teacher. He was patient with us as we asked a myriad of questions. He was also excited enough to see the birds himself that it really made the trip a journey. Unfortunately the air was smokey due to recent wildfires which made the birds less active, but we were still able to see plenty! This trip was well worth the time and price and I cannot wait to do it again in the future!! One of the owners (Teresa) also helped us later on in our trip. I was dying to see some condors. When we left Puerto Varas, heading to Santiago, she tried to book us a tour through the mountains with some friends of hers. Since it was so last minute she was not able to get us a guide but she was able to help us find a route and a look out point. We ended up sighting between 25 and 30 condors up close on the last day of our vacation. BirdsChile was so helpful the whole way through!

review_text: We did a 4 day tour from Atacama - Uyuni - Atacama with them last October. We already set our expectations low based on reviews and we actually had a great time. Our driver, Nelson was really great and made us feel comfortable during the whole trip and I think was one of the main reasons we enjoyed, apart from Bolivia being just gorgeous. It was a lot of combined effort by the lovely Bolivia locals, hotel employees, restaurant cooks, and the friendly drivers. The organizers however I think shouldn't be given too much credit. They weren't very helpful and responded late, when we were at their office in Atacama it was hard for them to even give a smile, there was even a guy on the desk who was rude to us, the guy in the Uyuni office wasn't too welcoming either and just left us clueless on what we'll do while waiting for our trip back. I also had an issue with a request I had, requesting them to connect us with the driver. Unfortunately we had a couple of photos taken on our driver's cellphone, he wasn't used to ours so he used his. Obviously I wanted the copies because we didn't have much, so I was patient and had weeks of back and forth emails with promises that they'll have it sent right away. A few months later I follow-up again and they just told me that they could no longer reach him and that he's left the company. How convenient. So really, Bolivia was/is amazing but I won't say it was because of the organizers. I suggest you book somewhere else as there are so many better options. When you get to San Pedro just do a quick walk and you'll find so many companies and you can even haggle for the prices.

review_text: A different look at Patagonia. Estancia Mercedes' owners welcome you like family and treat you with utmost hospitality. Farm-to-table breakfast, beef carpaccio and wine... and that's before the actual tour. You then get a crash course on horse riding and horses are selected according to your previous (or lack thereof) experience. You are then guided through rivers and forests. You're guaranteed to see some awesome views of flora and fauna. You can even pick up Calafates (berries) and taste them. You will get to the base of a rocky peak where condors nest. After some bird watching (and some more wine) you'll return to the family's home for a complete meal (beef, salad, home-made bread, potatoes...), all from their farm. A really great experience and a different approach to Patagonia. My only regret is not having more time to stay over at the Estancia for a couple of days. Thanks Eduardo for your honest opinion, it's good to know that you could appreciate the authenticity of our surroundings. We hope to see you again soon. Greetings from the whole family of Estancia Mercedes.

review_text: I bought with this agency the trips to Farellones and Portillo, taken by the suggestion of several travel influencers (which are sponsored, of course), the reviews on TripAdvisor and the good service via WhatsApp, what they offer is actually a good transport to the site, not a good tour experience. In addition, it is good to point out that the values of the tours are much higher than by other agencies. Well, the tour of Farellones was in a good quality van, however the Guide was quite sharp in some questions I made about the tour, in addition, isolated who bought tickets to the park online, even said that we should have bought in the clothes store, because it would harm him and there would be cheaper (the fact that did not happen, because the other travellers paid the same price). At the time we arrived in Farellones, he followed with those who bought tickets directly in the clothes shop, broke the queue of entrance to the park and let us see ships... We had to get help, because we bought through the site, but did not generate the tickets, it was a great effort to enter the park. For Portillo, the ride started wrong. There was a couple of Brazilians who were with us, who bought the tour to Farellones this day, they had already gone to Portillo the day before, and at the stop to the café they learned they were going back to Portillo, the agency confused and put them again on the tour of Portillo. Since there was no longer time for the van to pick them up for the scheduled tour, they had to go back to Portillo. Imagine you take a scheduled trip, and guys make a mistake like that? But finally, from the qualities of the Portillo tour, the picnic is very good and around. The van we went to is like those beasts, somewhat uncomfortable when it is overcrowded, yet, our Guide did not explain anything about the route, it looked shy, and we were knowing a little more about the place because the couple of Brazilians who had already gone to Portillo explained to us, otherwise we would leave without any knowledge about the place. After all, my suggestion is to search many agencies that are not commercial, so what I saw during the tours is that the smaller ones offer more attractive values and with guides who try more to bring a good experience to the vacationer.

review_text: Half a month of trekking in South America and this was the start. We frequently get to Colorado to hike in the mountains for weekends, so we supposed that we were trained. Not the case. With our w-trek tere were 3 days that killed our legs. No matter the pain (coincidence with "paine"), the nature and views were breathtaking (also the hike). By day and night, there was always the desire to just sit down and watch the mountains. By night we were lucky to have 3 nights with stars. If Peru, Bolivia or Chile, the sky looks very different than in the US. Ramon, who guided our small group with 2 couples and 3 solo travelers, as well as the team behind like our cook and the guys wearing our luggage. Respect to the entire team for the good job. The entire organization was very professional and also important, as during a hike like this a lot can go wrong. For hiking lovers this hike in the Paine National Park as well as the Inca Trail in Peru were the most challenging hikes of my life. My wife, fitter than I am, says the same.

review_text: Parque Quinta Normal is a great and relaxing place to go visit and have a boat ride. You can walk around and visit the museum that doesn't charge a fee. Also, you need to try out the sopiapillas (in the winter time) just walking around and eating them while they are hot! Don't wait until they get cold, they don't taste good. Another place if you are a book lover, there is the Santiago Library (Biblioteca de Santiago). As you walk out you will get close to Estacion Central, which is another great place to hang-out and just enjoy the place. In addition, the Planetarium is near by as well, if you like to enjoy a quiet evening watching the stars!

review_text: The day was amazing in tour to Valle Nevado! Regardless of the season - spring, we were awarded with snow, probably the last for 2014, escorted by good and friendly guys - tourist guides. After this great moment, we decided to buy a package from the same company to enjoy and traditional tourist dinner (never wait good food !). Unfortunately we were surprise with an unprepared guide, which started the tour with an awkward posture to speak for 16 Brazilians in Chilean Spanish (you know the the difference) and for a couple of American in English !! Looks for me that he does not know where the money come from !!!! Ok, could be my unwillingness, but in the restaurant he split my family - wife, daddy and mommy, both older than 85 years. I asked him to solve the issue (he just need to ask the American couple to switch one seat) and he replied "that's your your table, if you do not want I am sorry". The issue was solved after I talked to the restaurant manager, which promptly arranged another free table for us !! If you want to go to Valle Nevado do not hesitate ! If you want to have a boring dinner, ask whom will carry you ! Dear Fernando: We are very pleased that you enjoyed the tour to Valle Nevado with Turistik. However, we are concerned about what you comment about the dinner show. We would like to mention that most of our tours are in Spanish / English, yet our guides try their best to communicate with our Portuguese-speaking tourists. Anyway, we are concerned about what you told us that happened at the restaurant, this is why we would like you to email us at contacto@turistik.cl with the name of the guide and the day you did the tour. Of course we appreciate the information, and will investigate what happened.

review_text: Had 9 meals in this restaurant as stayed at the hotel for 4 days. Food:Breakfast- usual selection, bread is terrible- they need to sort as square loaf white or brown. The Nutella crep had too much Nutella in it. Lunch: had the two course lunch ( came with a small soup prior to the mains so more three courses) Three Course dinner menu- was good, had some interesting stuff such as ostrich. Service was super erratic- Cocktails are good but takes 20-30mins to arrive. Order a glass of wine prior. Some tables had their starters and mains come together if one had ordered both starters and mains and the other just the mains. At breakfast our order was given to the wrong table however they did not complaint so we had to wait another 20mins from then to get out cooked breakfast. Dinner was lovely as you see the sun set. The only time the food was average was during the BBQ on Tuesdays and Saturdays. Suggestion- number your tables and might find that orders get to the right place and fewer ordering errors.

review_text: Our whole family (3 children, 2 adults, 2 seniors) recently stayed at the Chile Nativo Riverside Camp and I wanted to write and share how impressed we all were with the location, but even more so the quality of the Chile Nativo staff in dealing with a medical emergency. First off, we loved the Riverside Camp, with great food, wonderful views, a great main dome to eat/relax, and charming canvas tents to stay in (with clean washrooms, heated blankets, power and more). What really impressed us was when my mother had medical issue that became a medical emergency and required treatment. The staff at the camp dropped what they were doing and were all well trained in first aid and helped with the issue. They also quickly alerted local park rangers who dispatched EMT's who came within 10 minutes. We subsequently evacuated to the Puerto Natales hospital, where another Chile Nativo staff member met my mother to act as an interpreter with the local doctors and nurses at the hospital. Our whole family is thankful for the training the team at the camp had, and it prevented a much more serious medical issue. So many thanks to the whole team. Thank you for sharing your experience. We’re glad to hear you enjoyed Riverside Camp and, most importantly, that our team was able to support you during a difficult moment. The safety and well-being of our guests are our top priorities, and we take pride in our staff’s quick and professional response. We’re relieved that your mother received the care she needed and grateful for the efforts of our team, park rangers, and medical staff. We’ll be sure to share your kind words with them. We hope to welcome you again under better circumstances. Wishing you all the best! The Chile Nativo Team

review_text: Arriving in his jeep straight to our hotel door, Guillermo welcomed us with an energetic wave and warm smile, taking us to Chepu to spend our day kayaking and hiking. On the way, we stopped off at a local’s homestead, to collect the kayaks and snacks for the trip ahead, spotting Chile’s famous pudú deer on the way! Kitted and ready to go, we set off – the scenes beheld were breath-taking! The result of a tsunami in the 60s, the trees lining Chepu river stand now as wooden bones emerging from the waters with sunlight beaming through, an ethereal ghost forest. Paddling upstream, we then moored on the bank for a break, we took in the beautiful wildlife including local black cormorants, in the surrounding forests of Chepu. Back on shore, we returned to the homestead, to be greeted with a log fire and traditional cuisine; amazing steak and potatoes, with a great vegetable platter for our vegetarian daughter. Whilst there, we got the opportunity to sample matte tea - a Chepu specialty. Richly infused, matte (mat-té) is herbal and bitter but once stirred with sugar and hot water, sweet and warming – a must-try! Changed out of our wet-gear, we took to the forest for a bushwalk, arriving in its depths by a mini train handmade by the homestead’s residents! With a vast knowledge of the fauna, Guillermo gave us an insightful tour of the forest, and led us down the river; crossing hanging bridges and stepping rocks as the river rushed by made this one eventful energetic trail! By the end, we were all worn out, falling asleep on the drive back to Castro, but couldn’t have asked for a better day, spent with great company. Bilingual, with an inspiring enthusiasm for the great outdoors, we can’t recommend Guillermo highly enough; we’ll definitely be calling on him again for our next adventure! We found Guillermo Retamal through TripAdvisor, on chilespotstourismo.com, then contacting him directly through his email chilespots@gmail.com. Find him also on Instagram @chilespots_travel! review_text: I saw the cerro everyday but it rained when we were there. Right across the road from the cerro is the souvenir market. Mainly local goods, such as woolens from Bolivia (scarves, jumpers etc), jewelry (lapis lazuli, coral, copper etc), and heaps of other random stuff, like bags, shoes - general souvenir stuff. Good place for cheap souvenirs and gifts. Open 10am but if it's wet most stall seem to open up later, after midday. They don't really haggle, we tried but if you buy a lot from the one place they'll drop the price. Plus many drop the price for paying in cash. Some places are desperate to make a sale they drop the price even if you are just looking to get you to buy. It's good if you want the stuff. Worth a visit. We did all our gift shopping here and good stuff can be found if you take time and look at it closely. There is also an empanda place and crepe/juice bar for a re-fuel. There is more eating options down the main road as well. Just next to the Santa Lucia metro station, exit San Isidro side, turn left when you get out of the stairs and follow the main road and you will see the market entry on the corner. Worth a stop if you need that kind of stuff. The park looked really pretty too, massive entry but like i said it was raining so we never went in.

There are 2 entrances, the closest to town is closed for entry after rains damaged the route but you can pay for your entrance here. Then you can cycle to the other entrance which is up a tough hill but with some breaks you'll get there. Best to do it early to avoid the heat! There is a class viewpoint at the 2nd entrance. There is also dunes to watch sandboarders! If you're lucky local dogs will follow you as well they know the area and are real friendly!! Awesome place and very cheap if you do it by bike!

review_text: We were booked by our tour company for a visit to see the Balmaceda, Serrano & Tyndall Glaciers & told to report at the quay side at 8.30 prompt. But there are 2 queys, both about 10 mins walk from the hotel, in opposite directions & the hotel did not know which one we should go to. After a slight panic a kind hotel worker discovered that we should really go to a house in the middle of a field! ( just so you know if you do this trip) There we were equipped with excellent spacesuit - like waterproofs which kept us warm & dry for our trip in the zodiac. My husband loved the whole experience, I was less enthusiastic as it started to rain heavily as soon as we set out & didn't stop till we got to the Serrano Glacier an hour later. On a dry day it would be a lovely journey. At the glacier there was a choice of an hours round trip to the base of the glacier on fairly rough terrain or a short easy walk to a view point looking over the water. I opted for the easy option, which was beautiful, & then sat in a comfortable boat till the others came back. There are welcome toilets at the stop. On the return journey we saw sea lions swimming by the zodiac , barking loudly, & Tyndall Glacier at a distance. Our helms man was skilled - we felt safe & well looked after. On return we were given an included lunch, which we hasn't expected, served with great care - delicious! The whole trip took 5 hours, not including getting dressed up in our suits . Good value & enjoyable.

review_text: Cajon del Maipo Embalse el Yeso was our first of two day tours booked with Stamps. IT WAS AMAZING!!! We received everything listed as included in the tour description, but what we didn’t necessarily expect to have included was our awesome tour guide Vanessa. She was so friendly, very knowledgeable about not only our excursion but also Santiago and Chile in general, and was just all around a very cool person. Cajon del Maipo was about an hour and a half drive from our hotel. Along the way we stopped at various sites to get pictures of the beautiful mountain scenery, during which Vanessa explained the significance of certain historical events in the region and answered any questions we asked. The drive to the top is not for the faint hearted, but she was a great driver and the tour company knew what kind of vehicle would be the best and smoothest ride. We passed several buses from other companies whose drivers and tourists looked a little uncomfortable trying to make it up the road. Upon arrival at Cajon del Maipo, we explored the breathtaking scenery and took incredible pictures, while Vanessa set up a full meal on a table and chairs in a spot overlooking the lake and mountains/glaciers. After our short hike to explore the area, we sat down to eat, drink wine, and enjoy good conversation. It was almost surreal to be in such an amazing place enjoying a simple but awesome meal. I’m definitely replicating the sandwiches with hearts of palm added when I get back to the states, so yummy! Everything was absolutely perfect from start to finish on this excursion, probably the most beautiful place I have ever seen, and our tour guide only made the day more wonderful. We ended the day thinking there was no way it could get any better. If you visit Cajon del Maipo and do not book through Stamps Tours, you’re definitely missing out!

review_text: My partner and I have climbed Volcan Villarrica about 5 times between the two of us and with 3 different companies, and this was by far the best experience we have had. We regularly visit the area with large groups of exchange students so we are always on the look out for the best guiding service for our groups, and we had heard good things about Summit Chile so we decided to give them a try when our usual tour company didn't have enough spots for all of our students. The guide to climber ratio was great--10 climbers with 4 guides, and not only that, but all of the guides were clearly very experienced, conscious of all safety precautions, and loved what they were doing (and I cannot say that about the other tour companies). We appreciated the fact that one guide led, another followed behind, and two guides constantly monitored the progess of the group by walking alongside climbers and offering suggestions and monitoring the group pace. All of the guides shared the philosophy that the experience should be fun, safe, and not leave you completely exhausted at the end of the day, whereas some other companies tend to take pride in arriving first at the top of the mountain or doing the climb in the shortest time possible. All other aspects were great--coordinating the visit, the high-quality equipment, transportation to and from our cabins at no extra cost, and even a free trip up the rock wall outside. Highly recommend Summit Chile; we will work with them again on any future group visits to Pucon.
